business_problem: Harvey needed a legal AI system that could reason over vast case-law and contract corpora with higher accuracy and fewer hallucinations than generic fine-tuning or basic retrieval could provide for professional legal work.
solution_summary: Harvey partnered with OpenAI to build a custom-trained model for legal professionals after finding that standard fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation could not reliably handle open-ended case-law research. The company combined its secure professional-services platform with a custom case-law model that injects large volumes of legal knowledge and domain-specific reasoning into the base model, first with Delaware case law and then across all U.S. case law. Harvey added the equivalent of 10 billion tokens of data and evaluated the system side by side against GPT-4 with attorneys from 10 major law firms. The resulting workflow helps lawyers ask complex research questions, draft documents, compare large contract sets, and receive longer answers grounded in citations, while Harvey continues exploring agent patterns that combine multiple model calls into more complete legal work products.

solution_components.name: Custom-trained case law model

data_flow: Lawyer questions and document-review tasks enter the Harvey platform, where the custom-trained case law model reasons over the added legal corpus and returns answers with supporting citations. Side-by-side evaluations and attorney feedback then inform further tuning of the model and future agent workflows.
business_outcome: Harvey improved legal-research quality and citation grounding, won strong attorney preference over baseline GPT-4 output, and created a foundation for broader drafting, contract analysis, and agent-assisted professional-services workflows.
